scenes.line1: Why do VM internet calls fail
scenes.say: Ever wonder why your virtual machines suddenly can't reach the internet when traffic spikes?

scenes.label: Options
scenes.sub: NAT Gateway, firewall, load balancer, or a VM's public IP.
scenes.say: VMs can reach the internet through a NAT gateway, a firewall, load balancer rules, or a public IP.
Each path shares a limited pool of SNAT ports. If your app opens lots of short-lived connections, those ports run out fast.

scenes.title: Check SNAT Usage
scenes.say: Check the SNAT connection count metric on your load balancer or NAT gateway. High failed counts mean port exhaustion.

scenes.question: What's the main cause of SNAT issues?
scenes.right: Too many new connections per request. Reuse connections instead.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: most SNAT problems are caused by apps opening new connections for every request, not just a lack of IP addresses.
